rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zajjaj identifies the honored servants as the angels and Jesus son of Mary.
rows.anchor: يعني الملائكة وعيسى ابن مريم عليه السلام

rows.speaker: التفسير
rows.claim: The interpretation transmitted in tafsir identifies the honored servants as angels.
rows.anchor: والذي في التفسير أنهم الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reading عبادا in the accusative is linguistically possible, meaning God took honored servants, but conflicts with the muṣḥaf; the nominative is better.
rows.anchor: ولو قرئت بل عبادا مكرمين لم يجز لمخالفة المصحف،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dual feminine verb is used because the heavens are expressed as one sky and the earths as one earth.
rows.anchor: لأن السماوات يعبر عنها بلفظ الواحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavens and earth were initially joined as one sky and one earth, without water; God split the sky into seven and made seven earths.
rows.anchor: كانتا سماء واحدة مرتتقة ليس فيها ماء

rows.speaker: التفسير
rows.claim: Tafsir says the sky was split by rain and the earth by vegetation.
rows.anchor: وجاء في التفسير أن السماء فتقت بالمطر، والأرض بالنبات

words: وَجَعَلْنَا مِنَ الْمَاءِ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ حَيٍّ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about making every living thing from water indicates that the sky's opening refers to rain.
rows.anchor: يراد بفتقها كون المطر فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ratq is a verbal noun, so it is used instead of the dual adjective ratqayn; the sense is that both had closure and were made open.
rows.anchor: لم يقل رتقين، لأن الرتق مصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account of creation demonstrates God's oneness and then rebukes the hearers for not believing.
rows.anchor: ودلهم بهذا على توحيده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means lest the earth move; Zajjaj prefers an implied genitive noun such as كراهة and says لا is not itself elided, though the result matches ألا تميد.
rows.anchor: المعنى كراهة أن تميد بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mayd means to turn or rotate; a passenger made seasick while riding the sea is called مائد.
rows.anchor: ومعنى تميد في اللغة تدور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rawasi means firmly fixed mountains.
rows.anchor: والرواسي تعني الجبال الثوابت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fijaj is the plural of fajj, a cleft between two mountains; subul means roads.
rows.anchor: فجاج: جمع فج، وهوكل منخرق بين جبلين، وسبلا: طرقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky is guarded from falling onto earth except by God's permission.
rows.anchor: حفظه الله من الوقوع على الأرض

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative explanation is that the sky is protected by the stars, as stated in the cited passage.
rows.anchor: وقيل محفوظا، أي محفوظا بالكواكب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing clause says that they turn away from God's signs.
rows.anchor: وهم عن آياتنا معرضون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yaʾjuj and Maʾjuj are read with hamza or without it; they are two tribes among God's creatures.
rows.anchor: بهمز وغير همز، وهما قبيلتان من خلق الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says that Yaʾjuj and Maʾjuj constitute nine of every ten human groups.
rows.anchor: ويروى أن الناس عشرة أجزاء تسعة منهم يأجوج ومأجوج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two names are foreign; a possible Arabic derivation links them to fire blazing (أججت) and to intensely salty, burning water (الأجاج).
rows.anchor: وهما اسمان أعجميان، واشتقاق مثلهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant has جدث with ج and ث, but Zajjaj judges the reading حدب with ح to be better.
rows.anchor: حدب ينسلون) بالحاء، والحدب كل أكمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadab is any hillock.
rows.anchor: والحدب كل أكمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yansilun means that they hurry or rush.
rows.anchor: والحدب كل أكمة، و (ينسلون) يسرعون

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some object that the waw cannot be omitted before the report of what the people say.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم: [لا يجوز طرح الواو] (2).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Basran reply supplies an omitted قالوا: after the opening of Gog and Magog and the approach of the true promise, they say their confession.
rows.anchor: والجواب عند البصريين قوله: (يا ويلنا قد كنا في غفلة من هذا)

rows.speaker: التفسير
rows.claim: Tafsir identifies the emergence of Gog and Magog as one of the signs of the Hour.
rows.anchor: وجاء في التفسير أن خروج يأجوج ومأجوج من أعلام الساعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading opens the عين in al-baʿth; the Kufans allow such vowel alternation in a quiescent second radical when it is a guttural and the first is open, citing pairs such as نعل/نعل and شعر/شعر.
rows.anchor: ويقرأ من البعث بفتح العين،

rows.speaker: البصريون
rows.claim: The Basrans say both forms are used only when both are attested; an unattested form such as وعد cannot be shifted, and the rule is not limited to guttural letters.
rows.anchor: فأما البصريون فيزعمون أن ما جاء

words: إِن كُنتُمْ فِي رَيْبٍ مِنَ الْبَعْثِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge to doubters is to reflect on their own creation: divine power has no difficulty originating life or bringing the dead back.
rows.anchor: فتدبروا أمر خلقكم وابتدائكم فإنكم لا تجدون في القدرة فرقا بين ابتداء الخلق وإعادته

words: مِن تُرَابٍ ثُمَّ مِن نُّطْفَةٍ ثُمَّ مِنْ عَلَقَةٍ ثُمَّ مِن مُّضْغَةٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stages are Adam created from dust, then his descendants created from a drop, a clot, and a morsel of flesh.
rows.anchor: خلقوا من تراب، وهو خلق آدم عليه السلام

words: مِن نُّطْفَةٍ ثُمَّ مِنْ عَلَقَةٍ ثُمَّ مِن مُّضْغَةٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the embryo remains a drop for forty days, then a morsel for forty days, after which an angel is sent to breathe in the spirit.
rows.anchor: ويروى أن الإنسان يكون في البطن نطفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mukhallaqa describes the created forms or stages.
rows.anchor: ومعنى (مخلقة وغير مخلقة) وصف الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some embryos complete the morsel stage and develop the organs that finish the human body's faculties, while others do not complete development.
rows.anchor: أو منهم من يتمم مضغته فتخلق له الأعضاء التي تكمل آلات الإنسان ومنهم من لا يتمم الله خلقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose clause refers to the account just given: God has described the stages of human creation.
rows.anchor: أي ذكرنا أحوال خلق الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, God created people in this way in order to make matters clear to them.
rows.anchor: ووجه آخر هو خلقناكم هذا الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb نقر is read only in the indicative nominative, not as a purpose coordinated with لنبين.
rows.anchor: لا يجوز فيها إلا الرفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It cannot mean that humans were created in order for God to keep embryos in wombs; human creation is for guidance and right conduct.
rows.anchor: لم يخلق الأنام لما يقر في الأرحام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although طفل is singular, it has the plural sense أطفال, as the address is plural; each person is brought out as a child.
rows.anchor: في معنى أطفال، ودل عليه ذكر الجماعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ashudd means full strength and discernment, reached between ages thirty and forty.
rows.anchor: تأويله الكمال في القوة والتمييز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The most decrepit age is the senility of old age, when a person loses reason, as the following clause explains.
rows.anchor: أرذل العمر هو الذي يخرف فيه الإنسان من الكبر حتى لا يعقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth is هامدة when dry and reduced to dust.
rows.anchor: يعني جافة ذات تراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth's shaking is its movement when water falls on it and it begins to grow vegetation.
rows.anchor: فاهتزازها تحركها عند وقوع الماء بها وإنباتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word is also read وربأت with hamza; the unhamzated reading derives from ربا يربو, to increase in any direction, while the hamzated form means it rose.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ: (وربت) فهو من ربا يربو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A bahij pair or kind means every beautiful species of plant.
rows.anchor: أي من كل صنف حسن من النبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhalika means the matter is as described; its syntactic position is best treated as nominative.
rows.anchor: أي الأمر ما وصف لكم وبين لكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It may instead be accusative, meaning God did this because He is the truth and revives the dead.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون نصبا على معنى فعل الله ذلك بأنه هو الحق وأنه يحي الموتى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will judge between the five named religious groups and the believers.
rows.anchor: يفصل الله بين هذه الفرق الخمس وبين المؤمنين

words: فَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا قُطِّعَتْ لَهُمْ ثِيَابٌ مِّن نَّارٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers receive garments of fire, while the believers enter gardens beneath which rivers flow.
rows.anchor: والمؤمنون يدخلون الجنة وهو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The predicate of the first إن is the following complete clause, which itself begins with إن الله يفصل.
rows.anchor: وخبر (إن) الأولى جملة الكلام

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some grammarians call إن زيدا إنه قائم poor, but accept the construction here because the first subject is a relative pronoun.
rows.anchor: زعم قوم أن قولك: إن زيدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zajjaj rejects a distinction between relative pronouns and other subjects: إن زيدا إنه قائم is good Arabic too.
rows.anchor: ولا فرق بين الذي وغيره في باب (إن)

rows.speaker: البصريون
rows.claim: The Basrans unanimously allow إن before any subject and predicate, with examples إن زيدا هو قائم and إن زيدا إنه قائم.
rows.anchor: وليس بين البصريين خلاف في أن " (إن) تدخل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed poet's line إن الخليفة إن الله سربله attests the repeated إن construction.
rows.anchor: إن الخليفة إن الله سربله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here prostration is submission and obedience to God by the created animate and inanimate; Zajjaj judges obedient prostration the strongest explanation.
rows.anchor: والسجود ههنا الخضوع لله عز وجل، وهى طاعة

words: وَكَثِيرٌ مِّنَ النَّاسِ وَكَثِيرٌ حَقَّ عَلَيْهِ الْعَذَابُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contrast between many people who prostrate and many on whom punishment is due supports taking سجود as obedience.
rows.anchor: والدليل على أنه سجود طاعة قوله: (وكثير من الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's command to heaven and earth to come willingly or unwillingly, and their answer that they came obediently, supports actual obedience by nonhuman creation.
rows.anchor: فقال لها وللأرض ائتيا طوعا أو كرها قالتا أتينا طائعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some stones fall from fear of God; Zajjaj argues that fear requires an attribute God has granted for testing their fear.
rows.anchor: يعني الحجارة (لما جهبط من خشية الله)

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some say the prostration of inanimate things and unreasoning animals is only the imprint of their maker and their creaturely subjection.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم: السجود من هذه الأشياء التي هي موات

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: An unnamed poet uses سجدا of hillocks humbled beneath horses' hooves, offered as evidence for the figurative view.
rows.anchor: ترى الأكم فيها سجدا للحوافر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zajjaj says the figurative view fails because God says some stones fear Him; He also says mountains and birds glorified with David, which would be oddly phrased if this were only created form.
rows.anchor: والذي يكسر هذا ما وصف الله عز وجل من أن من الحجارة لما يهبط من خشية الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountains' and birds' praise with David is real obedience, not merely an artifact of creation, since the created form is visible with David and others alike.
rows.anchor: فلو كان تسبيح الجبال والطير أثر الصنعة: ما قيل سخرنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zajjaj concludes that prostration, like the mountains' and birds' glorification, is obedient worship, though its manner is unknown without a report.
rows.anchor: فهو سجود طاعة لا محالة، وكذلك التسبيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that everything glorifies God, while people do not understand its glorification, is cited to support this unseen praise.
rows.anchor: وإن من شيء إلا يسبح بحمده ولكن لا تفقهون تسبيحهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الذين is genitive under an omitted أذن, meaning permission was given to those expelled from their homes.
rows.anchor: أذن للذين أخرجوا من ديارهم بغير حق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أن is genitive after the exception: they were expelled for no just cause except professing that God is their Lord.
rows.anchor: أخرجوا بلا حق، إلا بقولهم ربنا الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idol worshippers expelled the believers because they affirmed God's oneness.
rows.anchor: أي لم يخرجوا إلا بأن وحدوا الله

words: وَلَوْلَا دَفْعُ اللَّهِ النَّاسَ بَعْضَهُم بِبَعْضٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The implicit construction is لو لا أن دفع الله بعض الناس ببعض, had God not caused some people to repel others.
rows.anchor: ولولا أن دفع الله بعض الناس ببعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage also has a reading لهدمت; صوامع are monks' monasteries, بيع Christian churches, and صلوات Jewish synagogues, called ṣəlōtā in Hebrew.
rows.anchor: وتقرأ (لهدمت) وهي صوامع الرهبان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading has the singular صلاة; one explanation identifies the prayer sites as places of worship belonging to the Sabians.
rows.anchor: وقرئت صلاة ومساجد، وقيل إنها موضع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without mutual defense, every prophet's community would have seen its worship place demolished: synagogues in Moses' era, monasteries and churches in Jesus' era, and mosques in Muhammad's era.
rows.anchor: فكان لولا الدفع لهدم في زمن موسى عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God supports whoever upholds one of His revealed laws, while each prophet's law permits only what that prophet brought and forbids what he prohibited.
rows.anchor: أي من أقام شريعة من شرائعه، نصر على إقامة ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With accusative الفلك coordinates with ما, as if God subjected ships; تجري is a circumstantial clause describing them while running.
rows.anchor: (الفلك) بالنصب نسق - على " ما " المعنى وسخر لكم الفلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With nominative الفلك is the subject and تجري its predicate; ships' running by God's command still expresses subjection.
rows.anchor: ويقرأ: (والفلك تجري في البحر بأمره)، فيكون الفلك مرفوعا

words: وَيُمْسِكُ السَّمَاءَ أَن تَقَعَ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أن يقعَ is accusative as the object of يمسك, with the sense of holding the sky back lest it fall.
rows.anchor: على معنى كراهة أن تقع على الأرض، وموضع " أن " نصب بيمسك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zajjaj says he has already explained the word منسكا earlier.
rows.anchor: ومنسكا، وقد تقدم الشرح في هذا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command means do not argue or dispute with them; the following instruction for the case that they argue supports this sense.
rows.anchor: لا يجادلنك فيه، ومعناه لا تنازعهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This injunction precedes fighting, as indicated by the following direction about what to say if they argue.
rows.anchor: وإن جادلوك فقل الله أعلم بما تعملون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though they had already argued, the prohibition addresses the Prophet, telling him not to enter into a dispute with them.
rows.anchor: فالمعنى أنه نهي له - صلى الله عليه وسلم - عن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This reciprocal verb can forbid one side by saying لا يجادلنك فلان, equivalent to لا تجادلنه, because argument requires two participants.
rows.anchor: وهذا جائز في الفعل الذي لا يكون إلا من اثنين لأن المجادلة والمخاصمة لا تتم إلا باثنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same construction does not work with a nonreciprocal verb: لا يضربنك فلان cannot mean that you must not strike him; reciprocal لا يضاربنك can.
rows.anchor: لا يضربنك فلان، وأنت تريد لا تضربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant فلا ينزعنك means do not let them overpower you in the dispute.
rows.anchor: معناه لا يغلبنك في المنازعة فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zajjaj illustrates the verb with expressions for contending and defeating an opponent: نازعني فنزعته and عازني فعززته.
rows.anchor: نازعني فلان فنزعته وعازني فعززته

rows.speaker: أحمد بن حنبل
rows.claim: A report transmitted from Ahmad's Tafsir says God built Firdaws with alternating bricks of gold and silver and made its mountains of fragrant musk.
rows.anchor: روينا عن أحمد بن حنبل رحمه الله

rows.speaker: غيره
rows.claim: Another report says God swept Firdaws with His hand, built it of refined gold and scattered musk, and planted excellent fruit and fragrant basil there.
rows.anchor: وروينا عن غيره أن الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: سلالة has the morphological pattern فعالة; on this explanation, God created Adam from clay.
rows.anchor: سلالة: فعالة. فخلق الله آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the preceding interpretation, جعلناه refers to Adam's descendant.
rows.anchor: على هذا القول يعني ولد آدم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative says the clay-derived سلالة is Adam's semen.
rows.anchor: وقيل من سلالة من طين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sulalah is a small quantity of what is drawn off; words on فعالة such as الفضالة والنخالة والقلامة similarly denote a little remainder or shaving.
rows.anchor: وسلالة: القليل فيما ينسل. وكل

words: فَخَلَقْنَا الْمُضْغَةَ عِظَامًا فَكَسَوْنَا الْعِظَامَ لَحْمًا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Four forms are reported: plural عظاما/العظام, singular عظما/العظم, and both mixed combinations of singular and plural.
rows.anchor: وتقرأ على أربعة أوجه: أحدها ما ذكرنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Singular or plural is possible because a human has many bones; the singular can stand for the collective when context, including the flesh paired with bone, signals plurality.
rows.anchor: والتوحيد والجمع ههنا جائزان، لأنه يعلم أن الإنسان ذو عظام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed poet's singular عظم in في حلقكم عظم وقد شجينا means bones in your throats, illustrating a singular that denotes a plural.
rows.anchor: في حلقكم عظم وقد شجينا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One explanation of the new creation is that the child becomes male or female.
rows.anchor: فيه ثلاثة أقوال: قيل جعل ذكرا أو أنثى

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A second explanation is that the spirit is breathed into the child.
rows.anchor: وقيل نفخ فيه الروح

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A third explanation is that hair grows on the child.
rows.anchor: وقيل أنبت عليه الشعر

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: A report says Umar was with the Prophet when the verse was revealed and said the closing praise; the Prophet told Umar that God had ended the verse with those words.
rows.anchor: ويروى أن عمر كان عند رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both لمائتون and لميتون are allowed; لميتون is best and is the recited form, while مائتون suits the future.
rows.anchor: وأجودها (لميتون)، وعليها القراءة. وجاءت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seven paths are the seven heavens, each one a طريق.
rows.anchor: يعني به سبع سموات، فكل واحدة طريقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One sense is that God did not neglect to preserve the heavens, as in the verse calling the sky a guarded roof.
rows.anchor: أي لم نكن لنغفل عن حفظهن، كما قال: (وجعلنا السماء سقفا محفوظا)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, God created this world in order to preserve its creatures.
rows.anchor: وجائز أن يكون (وما كنا عن الخلق غافلين) أي إنا لحفظنا إياهم خلقنا هذا الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report identifies four rivers as coming from Paradise: the Tigris, Euphrates, Sayhan, and Jayhan.
rows.anchor: ويروى أن أربعة أنهار من الجنة، دجلة والفرات وسيحان وجيحان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The water was made fixed in the earth so that it does not depart.
rows.anchor: ومعنى (فأسكناه في الأرض) جعلناه ثابتا فيها لا يزول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Questions at the Resurrection are not requests for information but rebuke those responsible; God already knows and has recorded everything.
rows.anchor: وإنما تسأل لتوبيخ من قتلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lafḥ and nafaḥ have similar meanings, but lafḥ has the stronger effect.
rows.anchor: يلفح وينفح في معنى واحد، إلا أن اللفح أعظم تأثيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A kalih has lips drawn back from the teeth, like sheep's heads when fire exposes their teeth and shrivels their lips.
rows.anchor: والكالح الذي قد تشمرت شفته عن أسنانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word is also read شقاوتنا, with no change in meaning.
rows.anchor: وتقرأ شقاوتنا، والمعنى واحد (1).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They acknowledge that they were a people astray.
rows.anchor: وكنا قوما ضالين). أقروا بذلك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The innocent ones are Aisha and Safwan ibn al-Muʿattal, and by extension all believing men and women falsely accused by slanderers.
rows.anchor: أي عائشة وصفوان بن المعطل، وكذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The falsely accused receive forgiveness and generous provision, while slanderers face a curse in this world and the next and a great punishment.
rows.anchor: أي للذين قذفوا ورموا مغفرة ورزق كريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means that people pass the slander from one to another.
rows.anchor: معناه إذ يلقيه بعضكم إلى بعض

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha read تليقونه, which means rushing into falsehood.
rows.anchor: وقرأت عائشة رحمها الله: إذ تليقونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb ولق يلق means to hurry in lying or other matters; the poet's تلق witnesses this sense of hastening.
rows.anchor: يقال ولق يلق إذا أسرع في الكذب وغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Buyutan is read with ḍamma or kasra on the initial consonant; ḍamma is more common and follows the regular plural pattern, while Basrans judge the kasra very poor because fuʿul does not occur with initial kasra in Arabic.
rows.anchor: يقرأ بالضم والكسر، ولكن الضم أكثر، فمن ضم فعلى أصل الجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tastaʾnisu means seek permission, as in tafsir; istiʾdhan is seeking information or assurance.
rows.anchor: معنى تستأنسوا في اللغة تستأذنوا، وكذلك هو في التفسير، والاستئذان الاستعلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The related verbs آذن and آنس can mean inform and know, as in فإن آنستم منهم رشدا; therefore the phrase asks whether residents want the visitor to enter.
rows.anchor: تقول آذنته بكذا أي أعلمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next verse confirms that entry requires permission when nobody is found inside.
rows.anchor: والدليل على أنه الإذن قوله

words: بُيُوتًا غَيْرَ مَسْكُونَةٍ فِيهَا مَتَاعٌ لَّكُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Entry into certain uninhabited places is permitted without permission, including inns and commercial shops whose owners allow the public to enter.
rows.anchor: أي ليس عليكم جناح أن تدخلوا هذه بغير إذن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An inn is called a funduq or funtuq, with the consonant written or pronounced as د or ت.
rows.anchor: ويقال للخان فندق وفنتق. - بالدال والتاء -

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation identifies these places as ruins entered for urination or defecation.
rows.anchor: وقيل إنه يعني بها الخربات التي يدخلها الرجل لبول أو غائط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Matāʿ here means imtāʿ: a place where a person can relieve or benefit himself from his needs.
rows.anchor: ويكون معنى: (فيها متاع لكم) بمعنى إمتاع، أي متفرجون فيها مما بكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anbāʾ means reports or news; the disbelievers will learn its reality at the Resurrection, though some may be punished sooner, as at Badr.
rows.anchor: أنباء: أخبار. المعنى فسيعلمون نبأ ذلك في القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zawj means a kind, and karim means praiseworthy in its usefulness: beneficial species only the Lord of the worlds can grow and create.
rows.anchor: معنى زوج نوع، ومعنى كريم محمود فيما يحتاج إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The created things are signs that God is one and has no likeness.
rows.anchor: دليلا على أن الله - عز وجل - واحد وأن المخلوقات آيات تدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means that God knew most of them would never believe.
rows.anchor: معناه وما كان أكثرهم يؤمن، أي علم الله أن أكثرهم لا يؤمنون أبدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zajjaj compares the wording to ولا أنتم عابدون ما أعبد, which can describe both present and future nonworship.
rows.anchor: كما قال: (ولا أنتم عابدون ما أعبد) أي لستم تعبدون ما أعبد الآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God told Noah that none of his people would believe except those who had already believed, supporting the prediction about the majority.
rows.anchor: وكقوله في قصة نوح عليه السلام: (أنه لن يؤمن من قومك إلا من قد آمن)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إذ is accusative, governed by an understood command to recount this story as part of what is being recited.
rows.anchor: موضع (إذ) نصب، على معنى. . واتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The later command واتل عليهم نبأ إبراهيم confirms that this passage is to be recited as a story.
rows.anchor: ودليل ذلك قوله عطفا على هذه القصة: (واتل عليهم نبأ إبراهيم)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verbs are read with indicative رفع or subjunctive نصب; رفع, coordinated with أخاف, is the more common reading.
rows.anchor: بالنصب والرفع، فمن رفع فعطف على أخاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With رفع the phrase continues إني أخاف; with نصب it coordinates with أن يكذبون, as the feared consequences.
rows.anchor: ومن نصب فعطف على أن يكذبون، وأن يضيق صدري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses asks that Aaron be sent to help and support him; the purpose is omitted because the context makes it clear.
rows.anchor: أي ليعينني ويؤازرني على أمري، وحذف لأن في الكلام دليلا عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sin is the man Moses struck and killed; he fears they will kill him for that killing.
rows.anchor: يعني بالذنب الرجل الذي وكزه فقضى عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kalla is a rebuke and restraint against remaining in that fearful assumption, effectively telling Moses to trust God.
rows.anchor: كلا: ردع وزجر عن الإقامة على هذا الظن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine verb agrees with the collective sense جماعة قوم نوح, even though قوم is grammatically masculine.
rows.anchor: دخلت التاء وقوم نوح مذكرون، لأن المعنى كذبت جماعة قوم نوح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One possible reading is that Noah alone was denied; whoever rejects one of God's messengers rejects the whole company, since each messenger calls people to affirm all messengers.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكونوا كذبوا نوحا وحده، ومن كذب رسولا واحدا من رسل الله فقد كذب الجماعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another possible explanation is that Noah's people denied all the messengers.
rows.anchor: وجائز أن يكون كذبت جميع الرسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah is called their brother because he belonged to their people.
rows.anchor: وقيل (أخوهم) لأنه منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Messengers speak the language of their people so the proof will be established and made clearer to them.
rows.anchor: وكل رسول يأتي بلسان قومه ليوضع لهم الحجة ويكون أبين لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse is also read وأتباعك الأرذلون; this nominal form is linguistically strong because a circumstantial waw more often introduces nouns.
rows.anchor: ويقرأ (وأتباعك الأرذلون*، وهي في العربية جيدة قوية لأن واو الحال

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: Zajjaj illustrates nominal and verbal circumstantial constructions with جئتك وأصحابك الزيدون and جئتك وقد صحبك الزيدون; the latter verbal form is more common.
rows.anchor: لأنك تقول: جئتك وأصحابك الزيدون، ويجوز: وصحبك الزيدون، والأكثر جئتك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some say the elite called Noah's followers lowly because they worked as weavers, barbers, or in other trades; Zajjaj says occupations do not diminish religious standing.
rows.anchor: وقيل في قوله: الأرذلون: نسبوهم إلى الحياكة والحجامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threatened punishment is stoning with rocks.
rows.anchor: لتكونن من المرجومين (116) أي بالحجارة

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Fulk has the same form as singular and plural; Sibawayh compares it with أَسَد/أُسُد and notes plural forms such as أفلاك.
rows.anchor: واحدها فلك وجمعها فلك، وزعم سيبويه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mashḥun means filled; شحنته means I filled it.
rows.anchor: والمشحون المملوء، يقال شحنته أي ملأته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word rīʿ is read with kasra or fatḥa on rāʾ; both forms are mentioned.
rows.anchor: يقرأ ريع وريع - بكسر الراء وفتحها -

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A rīʿ is a raised place in the land; كم ريع أرضك asks how elevated the land is.
rows.anchor: وهو في اللغة الموضع المرتفع من الأرض ومن ذلك كم ريع أرضك

rows.speaker: التفسير
rows.claim: Tafsir explains بكل ريع as every mountain pass or, in another report, every road.
rows.anchor: جاء في التفسير: (بكل ريع) كل فج والفج الطريق المنفرج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Āyah here means a marker or sign.
rows.anchor: وجاء أيضا بكل طريق. وقوله (آية) علامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular of مصانع is مصنعة or مصنع; these are structures made to hold water.
rows.anchor: واحد المصانع مصنعة ومصنع، وهي التي تتخذ للماء

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation takes مصانع to mean buildings.
rows.anchor: واحد المصانع مصنعة ومصنع، وهي التي تتخذ للماء، وقيل مبان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They build as if seeking immortality, making structures for eternal life without reflecting on death.
rows.anchor: ومعنى (لعلكم تخلدون) أي لأن تخلدوا، أي وتتخذون مباني للخلود لا تتفكرون في الموت
